title: Derived global sections factors through affinization
statement: Let $X$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], put $A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and $Y=\operatorname{Spec} A$, and let $a:X\to Y$ be the canonical affinization morphism. With the unbounded derived categories [def-pc-derived-category], derived direct image [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image], and module-valued derived global sections [def-pc-global-derived-rhom], there is a natural isomorphism $R\Gamma(X,-)\cong R(\operatorname{Res}_{\gamma^{-1}}\circ\Gamma(Y,-))\circ Ra_*$, where we apply $Ra_*$ first, then the total right derived functor of global sections on $Y$ followed by restriction along $\gamma^{-1}:A\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$, with $\gamma=\Gamma\operatorname{Spec}Iso$. Both sides take values in $D(A)$. No compactness, quasi-separatedness, boundedness or quasi-coherence hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Lemma lemma-derived-pushforward-composition (Tag 0D5T), together with Section cohomology-unbounded (Tag 079V), module-valued global sections example

proof.text: Let P be the one-point ringed space with ring A, as in [def-pc-global-derived-rhom]. Let p:X → P have the identity on A, and let b:Y → P have ring map ΓSpecIso.inv:A → Γ(Y,O_Y). The Γ-Spec adjunction identity ΓSpecIso.inv ≫ a.appTop = id gives a ≫ b = p. On the empty open every sheaf of rings has its terminal zero ring, so this determines the entire ringed-space morphism. The identity is also valid when X is empty, when A is the zero ring.

Apply [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image-composition] to a and b, obtaining Ra_* ⋙ Rb_* ≅ Rp_*. This uses no exactness of module pullback and no flatness of a: the ringed-space theorem is the derived adjunction/composition theorem, not a claim that underived pushforward preserves K-injectivity.

The evaluation equivalence Mod(P) ≌ Mod(A) of [def-pc-global-derived-rhom] is exact. Compose its induced derived equivalence with the preceding comparison. It identifies Rp_* with RΓ(X,-); underived b_* followed by evaluation is Γ(Y,-) with scalars restricted along ΓSpecIso.inv. Postcomposition by an exact equivalence commutes with the total right derived construction, so Rb_* followed by derived evaluation is the right derived functor of that underived composite. Invert and compose the natural comparisons to obtain the asserted isomorphism. Naturality is inherited from the derived composition and exact-functor localization comparisons, hence holds on every unbounded derived object.

theorem derivedGlobalSections_affinization_comparison (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wX} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wY}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (Spec Γ(X, ⊤)).toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wA}
      (ModuleCat.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤)))] :
    letI : HasDerivedCategory.{wA} (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, ⊤)) :=
      inferInstanceAs (HasDerivedCategory.{wA}
        (ModuleCat.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤))))
    Nonempty ((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).rightDerivedFunctor ≅
      schemeDerivedDirectImage X.toSpecΓ ⋙
        (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor (Spec Γ(X, ⊤)).toRingedSpace ⋙
          ModuleCat.restrictScalars (Scheme.ΓSpecIso Γ(X, ⊤)).inv.hom).rightDerivedFunctor)
